metadata.purpose: Validate Scientific Reflow generalizability to XPCS dynamics measurements at 11-ID CHX

reference_paper.title: Domain switching dynamics in ferroelectric crystals using X-ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy

metadata.validation_approach: Model XPCS experiment (Systems A-F), run gap closure, infer domain relaxation timescale from g2(q,τ) correlation function

validation_strategy.description: We will treat the ferroelectric crystal as having PARTIALLY_KNOWN properties (crystal structure and static domain structure known, domain dynamics and relaxation timescales UNKNOWN), then use gap closure to see if we can infer the domain switching timescale from XPCS correlation function g2(q,τ).
known_beforehand: Crystal structure: Perovskite structure (BaTiO3 or similar)
Coercive field: ~1-5 kV/cm (field needed for domain switching)
discovered_by_experiment: Critical slowing down near coercive field
validation_strategy.gap_closure_target: Can we infer the domain relaxation timescale (τ_relax ~ 10-1000 ms) from the XPCS correlation function g2(q,τ)?
validation_strategy.success_criteria: Gap closure should propose: (1) Domain relaxation timescale in ms-sec range, (2) Timescale increases near coercive field (critical slowing), (3) Dynamics are driven by electric field

experimental_components.description: High-coherence undulator optimized for XPCS measurements at CHX beamline
experimental_functions: Generate coherent hard X-ray beam for XPCS
Provide spatial coherence for speckle pattern formation
Enable time-resolved dynamics measurements
experimental_components.notes: COHERENCE IS CRITICAL - High transverse coherence enables sharp speckle patterns for correlation analysis

experimental_components.description: Specialized optics designed to preserve wavefront coherence for XPCS

physical_properties.focusing: Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors or beryllium compound refractive lenses (CRLs)
physical_properties.wavefront_preservation: Minimal phase distortions (critical for speckle quality)
physical_properties.working_distance: Compatible with electric field cell geometry

experimental_functions: Select X-ray energy (9 keV for ferroelectric samples)
Preserve wavefront coherence for speckle formation
Focus beam onto sample without introducing aberrations
experimental_components.notes: Coherence preservation is CRITICAL - Any wavefront distortion degrades speckle contrast and correlation analysis

experimental_components.description: Custom cell for applying electric fields to ferroelectric sample during XPCS measurements

physical_properties.cell_type: Parallel-plate capacitor geometry with X-ray transparent electrodes
physical_properties.electrode_material: Indium tin oxide (ITO) or thin metal films (X-ray transparent)
physical_properties.field_orientation: Parallel or perpendicular to ferroelectric polarization axis
physical_properties.temperature: Room temperature (~298 K) or variable (200-400 K)
physical_properties.time_resolution: Electric field can be pulsed or ramped (ms-sec timescale)

experimental_functions: Apply electric field to drive domain switching
Control domain dynamics (field strength, direction, pulse duration)
Enable in-situ XPCS measurements during domain evolution
experimental_components.notes: DYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT - Electric field drives domain switching, creating time-dependent structural fluctuations measured by XPCS

experimental_components.description: Ferroelectric perovskite crystal with UNKNOWN domain dynamics and relaxation timescales

physical_properties._comment_known: KNOWN properties (from diffraction, microscopy, bulk measurements)
physical_properties.domain_wall_velocity: UNKNOWN (GOAL: infer from timescale and domain size)

experimental_components.gap_closure_goal: Infer domain relaxation timescale τ_relax from XPCS correlation function g2(q,τ) = A·exp(-2t/τ) + 1

constraints.timescale_range: Domain dynamics expected in ms-sec range (10^-3 to 10^0 s)
constraints.electric_field_dependence: Timescale decreases with increasing field (faster switching)
constraints.critical_slowing: Timescale diverges near coercive field (Ec ~ 1-5 kV/cm)
constraints.domain_size_constraint: Domain wall velocity v ~ domain_size / τ_relax

experimental_functions: Scatter coherent X-rays to produce speckle pattern
Evolve domain structure under applied electric field
Generate time-dependent speckle fluctuations encoding domain dynamics
experimental_components.notes: THIS IS SYSTEM D - THE KNOWLEDGE GAP. Domain dynamics (relaxation time, switching mechanism) are UNKNOWN and will be inferred from g2(q,τ).

experimental_components.description: Fast photon-counting area detector for time-resolved XPCS speckle pattern acquisition

physical_properties.dynamic_range: Up to 10^6 photons per pixel (16-bit or 32-bit)

experimental_functions: Acquire time-series of speckle patterns I(q,t) at kHz frame rate
Resolve speckle fluctuations on ms-sec timescales
Enable pixel-wise time correlation analysis for g2(q,τ)
Provide spatial resolution for q-dependent dynamics

measured_observables.primary_observable: Time-series of 2D speckle intensity patterns I(q,t)

experimental_components.notes: CRITICAL MEASUREMENT - Fast detector captures speckle pattern evolution. Timescale of g2(q,τ) decay encodes domain relaxation dynamics.

experimental_components.description: Computational pipeline to calculate time autocorrelation function g2(q,τ) from speckle pattern time-series

physical_properties.input_data: Time-series of 2D speckle patterns I(q,x,y,t), 4M pixels × 10^4 frames ~ 40 GB
physical_properties.output_data: Correlation function g2(q,τ) and relaxation timescale τ_relax
physical_properties.q_averaging: Azimuthal averaging for isotropic systems, or sector analysis for anisotropic
physical_properties.real_time_processing: Streaming analysis during acquisition (skbeam, PyXPCS libraries)
physical_properties.data_reduction: g2(q,τ) is ~1000× smaller than raw data (10^4 τ points vs 10^6 frames)

experimental_functions: Calculate temporal autocorrelation function g2(q,τ) from speckle patterns
Fit exponential decay to extract relaxation timescale τ_relax(q)
Generate two-time correlation maps C(t1,t2) for non-stationary dynamics
Identify dynamics regimes (ballistic, diffusive, arrested)
Detect critical slowing near coercive field

computational_properties.processing_time: Minutes to hours (depending on dataset size)

experimental_components.notes: THIS IS SYSTEM F - REQUIRED for XPCS. Converts raw speckle patterns I(q,t) → g2(q,τ) → τ_relax. Without System F, XPCS data is uninterpretable.

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: Coherent X-ray generation and wavefront propagation
physical_interactions.interaction_strength: Coherent flux ~10^11-10^12 ph/s, transverse coherence ~10 μm
physical_interactions.description: Undulator generates spatially coherent X-ray beam, optics preserve coherence for speckle formation

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: Coherent X-ray scattering from ferroelectric domains, speckle pattern formation
physical_interactions.interaction_strength: Scattered intensity I(q) ~ domain structure factor |F(q)|^2
physical_interactions.description: Coherent beam scatters from domain structure, producing characteristic speckle pattern encoding domain configuration

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: Electric field drives domain wall motion and domain switching
physical_interactions.interaction_strength: Applied field 0-10 kV/cm, domain wall velocity v ~ 10-1000 μm/s
physical_interactions.description: Electric field drives domain switching, creating time-dependent domain evolution measured by XPCS

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: Time-dependent speckle pattern fluctuations from domain dynamics
physical_interactions.interaction_strength: Scattered intensity I(q,t) fluctuates with timescale τ_relax ~ 10-1000 ms

measured_data.timescale_signature: Speckle decorrelation time τ_relax encodes domain relaxation
measured_data.electric_field_dependence: τ_relax decreases with increasing field (faster switching)
measured_data.critical_slowing: τ_relax diverges near coercive field Ec
measured_data.q_dependence: τ_relax(q) may vary with length scale (domain size, domain wall thickness)

physical_interactions.description: THIS IS THE CRITICAL DATA - Time-series of speckle patterns I(q,t). Decorrelation timescale encodes domain dynamics.

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: Pixel-wise temporal autocorrelation calculation from frame sequence
physical_interactions.interaction_strength: Computational: 4M pixels × 10^4 frames → g2(q,τ) at 10^3 q-points
physical_interactions.description: System F computes g2(q,τ) from I(q,t) time-series. Exponential decay g2 ~ exp(-2τ/τ_relax) reveals domain relaxation time.

domain_relaxation_timescale.value: τ_relax ~ 10-100 ms (typical for ferroelectric domain switching)
domain_relaxation_timescale.interpretation: Domain walls move with velocity v ~ domain_size/τ_relax ~ 1-10 μm/s

electric_field_dependence.description: τ_relax decreases with increasing electric field (exponential or power-law)
electric_field_dependence.critical_slowing: τ_relax diverges near coercive field Ec ~ 1-5 kV/cm (critical dynamics)

switching_mechanism.description: Domain switching occurs via nucleation and growth of reverse domains
switching_mechanism.dynamics_type: Activated process (Merz law: τ ~ exp(E_a / E) )

heterogeneity.description: Spatial heterogeneity in dynamics (faster near defects, slower in bulk)

measured_observables: Time-series of speckle patterns I(q,t) shows fluctuations with timescale τ_relax
Correlation function g2(q,τ) = β·exp(-2τ/τ_relax) + 1 decays with characteristic time
Electric field E controls dynamics (faster switching at higher E)
gap_closure_configuration.matrix_formulation: Infer System D (domain dynamics τ_relax) from measured D→E interaction (speckle fluctuations) and E→F interaction (g2(q,τ) analysis) given known A, B, C, E, F
gap_closure_configuration.expected_outcome: Gap closure should propose: (1) Domain relaxation timescale τ_relax ~ 10-100 ms, (2) Timescale decreases with E-field, (3) Critical slowing near Ec

success_criteria.timescale_range: Gap closure proposes relaxation time in ms-sec range (10^-3 to 10^0 s)
success_criteria.electric_field_dependence: Gap closure identifies faster dynamics at higher E-field
success_criteria.critical_slowing_detected: Gap closure recognizes timescale divergence near coercive field
success_criteria.physical_plausibility: Domain wall velocity v = domain_size/τ_relax is physically reasonable (1-1000 μm/s)

comparison_to_published.published_mechanism: Nucleation-growth with critical slowing near Ec
comparison_to_published.verdict: TBD (PASS if timescale within order of magnitude and mechanism qualitatively correct)

similarities: System D is PARTIALLY_KNOWN (target of discovery)
Gap closure goal is to infer System D properties
differences: System A: Coherent undulator (spatial coherence critical) vs EPU49 (RIXS) or wiggler (XAS)
System B: Coherence-preserving optics vs energy-resolution optics (RIXS) or high-flux optics (XAS)
System C: Electric field cell (dynamic) vs cryostat (RIXS, static) or electrochemical cell (XAS, dynamic)
System E: Fast area detector (kHz, speckle imaging) vs RIXS spectrometer (energy-resolved) or fluorescence detector (XAS)
System F: REQUIRED for XPCS (correlation analysis), REQUIRED for XAS (async DAQ), NOT NEEDED for RIXS
Time domain: Millisecond dynamics (XPCS) vs seconds-hours (XAS operando) vs static (RIXS)
Observable: g2(q,τ) correlation function (XPCS) vs μ(E,t) absorption (XAS) vs I(ΔE) energy loss (RIXS)
comparison_to_rixs_and_xas_cases.key_insight: Systems A-E are generalizable across all three techniques. System F is REQUIRED for time-resolved (XAS) and correlation-based (XPCS) measurements, NOT NEEDED for static energy-resolved (RIXS).

notes.validation_approach: This test validates that Scientific Reflow can handle time-correlation techniques (XPCS). If gap closure successfully infers the domain relaxation timescale from g2(q,τ), it confirms the Systems A-F architecture is universal across beamlines.
notes.system_f_critical: System F is ABSOLUTELY CRITICAL for XPCS. Without correlation analysis, raw speckle patterns I(q,t) contain no interpretable dynamics information. g2(q,τ) is the measurable observable that encodes System D dynamics.
notes.challenge: XPCS analysis is computationally intensive (pixel-wise correlations over millions of frames). Gap closure must recognize that g2(q,τ) exponential decay directly encodes System D relaxation time. Unlike RIXS (static) or XAS (time-resolved state), XPCS measures FLUCTUATION timescales.
notes.next_steps: After running this validation alongside RIXS (2-ID) and XAS (8-ID), we can definitively conclude if Systems A-F architecture is beamline-agnostic with configuration profiles.
